note: The shaft's three levels reach about 30 m below the Khafre causeway, with water standing in the lowest. Depth below its own ground, the causeway's surface, not below the pyramid's base plane: the two grounds differ, and nothing here places the causeway's level, so the figure that shows it says each depth is from its own ground. 'About' is the source's. Entered from the structure's register note, which came from the secondary literature; the page is not yet recorded, so unverified.

A seismic refraction anomaly in front of the forepaws, read by the authors as a possible cavity about 5 m below the floor of the Sphinx enclosure. Never excavated. Depth below the enclosure floor, not below the pyramid's base plane. Entered from the structure's register note; the paper's page and figure are not yet recorded, so unverified.

Four 4-inch boreholes, PZ/S1 to S4, drilled early in 2008 by the SCA and Cairo University's Engineering Center for Archaeology and Environment '20 meters (66 feet) deep into the bedrock' around the Sphinx, to watch the groundwater; cameras were lowered into them, and no log of the rock has been published. Depth below each hole's own ground, about the enclosure's level by the printed elevations. Entered from the source's register note (pp. 1 to 2), which came from the chapter 8 research job; not yet checked against the page here, so unverified.

Seismic refraction under the floor of the Sphinx's ditch (Dobecki and Schoch 1992), as Schoch gave the depths in KMT in 1992 and as Reader's Fig. 5 caption repeats them (checked on academia.edu): the depth of the low-velocity layer, read by Schoch as the rock weathered since the floor was cut. Below the ditch floor, not the pyramid's base plane. The paper's own tables, lines and sigmas are not yet read, so unverified; no sigma is entered because none is given where it was read. In front of the Sphinx and along its sides, lines S1, S2 and S4: 1.8 to 2.5 m; this is the shallow end. Reader adds that S4 approaches 4 m at one point.
